instructions:
GOAL: Raise the weapon maximum level from 3 to 5 everywhere it is hardcoded, and replace the current flat `damageForLevel` curve with a data-driven per-level scaling model so leveling from 1 to 5 is deterministic and the level-up draft keeps offering an 'upgrade this weapon' card until the weapon reaches level 5.

IMPORTANT PATH CORRECTION: The task lists `src/sim/upgrades.ts`, but in this repo that file does not exist. The real draft/upgrade logic lives in `src/sim/systems/upgrades.ts` (re-exported through `src/sim/index.ts`). Edit `src/sim/systems/upgrades.ts` wherever these instructions say 'the upgrades system'. Do NOT create a new `src/sim/upgrades.ts`.

GROUNDING (read before editing):
- `src/sim/data/weapons.ts` — defines `interface WeaponDef` with the field `maxLevel: 3` (a LITERAL type `3`, not `number`), the `WEAPON_POOL` array (9 weapons, each currently `maxLevel: 3`), and `export function damageForLevel(def, level)` which returns `def.baseDamage * (1 + 0.5 * (level - 1))`.
- `src/sim/systems/upgrades.ts` — `buildLevelDraft` and `buildChestDraft` both push a `weapon:lvl:<id>` candidate only when `(slot.level ?? 1) < 3`; `applyUpgradePick` only increments a slot's level when `(slot.level ?? 1) < 3`. These two `< 3` guards are the level cap and both must become `< 5`.
- `src/sim/state.ts` — `interface EquippedWeapon { weaponId; level: number; timer; rarity? }`. The comment there says `level: 1-3`; update the comment to `1-5`. Do NOT change the field type (it is already `number`).
- `src/sim/systems/weapons.ts` — `weaponSystem` fires each slot and computes damage via `damageForLevel(def, slot.level ?? 1)`. Spread/explosive behaviors currently spawn a FIXED number of projectiles (e.g. `spread-nearest` fires exactly 3, `straight-up` fires 1). Any 'add a projectile' mechanic at level 2/4 must be applied HERE by reading the slot level.
- `src/render/levelup.ts` — `resolveCardInfo` builds the 'Upgrade: <name>' card text with the hardcoded string `` `Lv${curLv} -> Lv${curLv + 1}  (+50% dmg)` ``. This description is now wrong and must be regenerated from the new scaling model (see below).
- `src/render/hud.ts` — the HUD stats label does NOT currently show weapon levels; no change strictly required, but if you add any weapon-level display it must read `s.player.weapons[i].level` and clamp display to 5.
- Determinism: sim is seeded (`s.rng`). NO `Math.random`, `Date.now`, or `performance.now` in `src/sim/`. `test/sim-purity.ts` enforces this — keep all new sim math pure and seeded.

DATA MODEL (author this in `src/sim/data/weapons.ts`):
1. Change the `WeaponDef` field `maxLevel: 3` to `maxLevel: number` (widen the literal type) and set every `WEAPON_POOL` entry's `maxLevel` to `5`. (Widening the type is required because a literal `3` would make `maxLevel: 5` a type error.)
2. Define a per-level scaling model. Author it as an exported table so it is data-driven and deterministic:
   - Add `export interface WeaponLevelMods { damageMul?: number; extraProjectiles?: number; extraAoe?: number; }` describing the CUMULATIVE (level-1-relative) modifiers a weapon has AT a given level.
   - Add `export const DEFAULT_LEVEL_MODS: WeaponLevelMods[]` indexed by level (index 0 unused or level-1 baseline). Follow the GDD cadence: level 1 = baseline; level 2 = a mechanical tweak (`extraProjectiles: 1` OR `extraAoe: 20` — pick per weapon family, see step 3); level 3 = damage bump (`damageMul: 1.5`); level 4 = another mechanical tweak (a further `extraProjectiles: 1` / `extraAoe`); level 5 = damage bump (`damageMul: 2.0`). Make the mods CUMULATIVE so `damageMul` at level 5 already includes the level-3 gain (e.g. lvl1 mul 1.0, lvl2 1.0, lvl3 1.5, lvl4 1.5, lvl5 2.0; extraProjectiles lvl1 0, lvl2 1, lvl3 1, lvl4 2, lvl5 2).
   - Add an OPTIONAL per-weapon override: extend `WeaponDef` with `levelMods?: WeaponLevelMods[]` so a specific weapon can diverge from the default curve. Weapons without it use `DEFAULT_LEVEL_MODS`.
   - Add `export function levelModsFor(def: WeaponDef, level: number): WeaponLevelMods` returning `(def.levelMods ?? DEFAULT_LEVEL_MODS)[Math.max(1, Math.min(level, def.maxLevel))]` (clamp to [1, maxLevel]).
3. Rewrite `damageForLevel` to use the table: `return def.baseDamage * (levelModsFor(def, level).damageMul ?? 1);`. This MUST remain a pure function of (def, level). Verify the values are monotonic non-decreasing in level for every weapon (levels 3 and 5 strictly increase damage; levels 2 and 4 keep damage flat but add a mechanic).
   - Because damage now only rises at levels 3 and 5 (not every level), the existing test `test/sim.weapons.ts` assertions `dmgLvl2 > dmgLvl1` and `dmgLvl3 > dmgLvl2` will need review — see ACCEPTANCE/TESTS below. Keep `damageForLevel(def,1)` == `def.baseDamage` exactly (multiplier 1.0) so no other test regresses.

MECHANIC APPLICATION (in `src/sim/systems/weapons.ts`):
- Read `const mods = levelModsFor(def, slot.level ?? 1)` once per slot fire.
- For `spread-nearest` and `spread-explosive`: fire `3 + (mods.extraProjectiles ?? 0)` projectiles total, fanning the extra projectiles out at additional +/- `SPREAD_DELTA` increments (keep the existing 3 center/right/left, then add symmetric pairs for each extra). Keep it deterministic — no rng in the fan geometry.
- For `aoe-nearest`: widen the blast by `mods.extraAoe ?? 0` px (i.e. `AOE_RADIUS + (mods.extraAoe ?? 0)`), so the level-2/4 mechanic is a bigger AoE.
- For `straight-up` / `straight-up-explosive`: apply `extraProjectiles` by firing that many additional straight shots with a small deterministic angular offset (or additional explosive shots), OR if you prefer to keep those single-shot, give those weapons a `levelMods` override whose level-2/4 mechanic is `extraAoe`/`damageMul` instead of `extraProjectiles`. Either is acceptable as long as leveling those weapons still visibly changes behavior and stays deterministic.
- Do NOT change `cooldown` scaling here (out of scope).

DRAFT / CAP CHANGES (in `src/sim/systems/upgrades.ts`):
- In BOTH `buildLevelDraft` and `buildChestDraft`, change the weapon-level candidate guard from `if ((slot.level ?? 1) < 3)` to `if ((slot.level ?? 1) < def.maxLevel)` — look up `def` from `WEAPON_POOL` (or hardcode `< 5` only if a lookup is awkward; prefer `def.maxLevel` so evolved weapons in spec #2 stay compatible).
- In `applyUpgradePick`, change the `weapon:lvl:` branch guard from `if (slot && (slot.level ?? 1) < 3)` to `if (slot && (slot.level ?? 1) < <that weapon's maxLevel>)` (look up the def; fall back to 5). Increment `slot.level` by 1 as today.
- The fusion path in `buildLevelDraft` currently requires `wA.level === 3 && wB.level === 3` (see `eligiblePairs`). With max level now 5, fusion should require MAX level, so change these to `wA.level === wA-def.maxLevel && wB.level === wB-def.maxLevel` (i.e. both at their own max, which is 5 for base weapons). Mirror the same change in `src/sim/systems/fusion.ts` `fuseWeapons` where it checks `if (wA.level !== 3 || wB.level !== 3) return false;` -> compare against each weapon's `maxLevel`. This keeps fusion as a 'both maxed' gate rather than a literal 3. (If you leave fusion at literal 3 the fusion tests will pass but fusion becomes reachable before a weapon is maxed, contradicting the GDD; changing to maxLevel is the correct behavior.)

RENDER / UI (in `src/render/levelup.ts`):
- In `resolveCardInfo`, for the `weapon:lvl:` case, regenerate the description from the new model instead of the hardcoded `(+50% dmg)` string. Compute `nextMods = levelModsFor(def, curLv + 1)` and describe the delta: if the next level increases `damageMul` vs the current level, show the damage delta (e.g. `+50% dmg` when 1.0->1.5, `+33% dmg` when 1.5->2.0 — or simply show the resulting multiplier); if the next level adds `extraProjectiles`, show `+1 projectile`; if it adds `extraAoe`, show `+AoE`. Always show the `Lv${curLv} -> Lv${curLv+1}` prefix. Cap the displayed target at 5. Import `levelModsFor` (and any needed types) from `src/sim/data/weapons.ts`.
- The draft UI already only ever renders 3 cards from `s.pendingUpgrades` (the pool draws 3), so no new card slots are needed for 5 levels — leveling to 5 just means the `weapon:lvl:` option keeps appearing across successive drafts until the weapon hits 5. Confirm the card still renders correctly when `curLv` is 4 (shows `Lv4 -> Lv5`).
- If you added a weapon-level readout to `src/render/hud.ts`, clamp it to 5 and label it (e.g. `axe Lv5`). Optional.

ACCEPTANCE (deterministic; gate = `npm run gate` = `tsc --noEmit` + canary + determinism + sim-purity + sim + budget):
1. `tsc --noEmit` passes (the `maxLevel` literal widening is why this compiles).
2. For a fixed seed, a single weapon can be leveled 1->5 via repeated `applyUpgradePick` on a `weapon:lvl:<id>` id, and `slot.level` ends at exactly 5 and cannot exceed 5 (attempting a 6th level-up is a no-op).
3. `damageForLevel(def, 5) > damageForLevel(def, 3) > damageForLevel(def, 1)` for every weapon, and `damageForLevel(def, 2) === damageForLevel(def, 1)`, `damageForLevel(def, 4) === damageForLevel(def, 3)` (damage only rises at 3 and 5). Value is a pure function of (def, level) — same inputs always same output.
4. `test/determinism.ts` (seed 9001, 1200 ticks, drains the seeded auto-pick each tick) still produces byte-identical checkpoints across two runs. Since leveling now changes projectile counts/AoE, the golden snapshots WILL differ from the pre-change run, but the two runs within the test must match each other — that is what the test asserts (it recomputes both runs live, no committed golden file), so it stays green as long as your sim math is pure/seeded.
5. `test/sim-purity.ts` stays green (no `Math.random`/`Date.now`/`performance.now` added to `src/sim/`).

TESTS TO UPDATE (REQUIRED — these currently assert the level-3 cap and WILL fail otherwise; updating them is part of this task):
- `test/sim.weapons.ts`: (a) the block that sets `sCap.player.weapons[0].level = 3` then asserts it stays capped at 3 — change to set level to 5 and assert it stays capped at 5. (b) The `dmgLvl2 > dmgLvl1` / `dmgLvl3 > dmgLvl2` assertions — change to the new curve reality: assert `damageForLevel(def,3) > damageForLevel(def,1)` and `damageForLevel(def,5) > damageForLevel(def,3)` (and that lvl2 equals lvl1). (c) The fusion setup blocks that build weapons at `level: 3` to test fusion — bump them to `level: 5` (their own max) so `fuseWeapons` still succeeds after the maxLevel gate change. Update every `level: 3` used as a 'maxed for fusion' fixture to `level: 5`; leave unrelated `level: 2` fixtures alone.
- `test/sim.upgrades.ts`: the `sCap` block that sets `weapons[0].level = 3` and asserts cap at 3 -> set to 5, assert cap at 5. The draft-fusion block sets `level: 3` on axe+knives to make them fusion-eligible -> bump to `level: 5`. Keep all other assertions.
- Do NOT weaken any assertion just to make it pass — update it to reflect the new max-level-5 reality.

OUT OF SCOPE: tiers/evolution (that is spec #2 `weapon_evolve_tiers.txt`). Do not add `tier`/`evolvesTo` here. Do not touch chest spawning. Do not change cooldowns.
